National Assembly
Twenty-first Session
Complete Minutes of Proceedings
26 Ashadh, 2083 Friday
Meeting Number- 32
Today's meeting of the National Assembly commenced at 13:19 hrs under the chairmanship of the Honourable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable members, the meeting proceedings are commencing. Honourable members, time has been requested to speak during the zero hour. A time limit of 3 minutes has been set for speaking during the zero hour. Honourable Mr. Padam Bahadur Pariyar.
Honourable Mr. Padam Bahadur Pariyar (Nepali Congress):- Honourable Chairperson, today the country is weeping. The promising Nepali youth Ganesh Nepali from Mugu has recently passed away. Yesterday, due to the state's crackdown, unconstitutional actions, and attempts to illegally apprehend him in Tripureswor, a promising youth lost his life. I want to ask the state, did you rescue Ganesh Nepali, or did you apprehend Ganesh Nepali and take him to the hospital? I want to express my regret for the fact that without any humanity, without even a shred of compassion, he was treated like a criminal, his body was burned, and then dragged like a criminal by the police and taken to the hospital. I want to ask the government, even before you came to power, even before your government was formed, many poor people's houses have been demolished, many poor people have been rendered destitute, Dalits have lost their lives. Today, three Dalits have lost their lives in government custody, they have lost their lives in the presence of the government. Therefore, I want to ask the government, this kind of excess cannot continue. If the government continues to proceed in such an inhumane manner towards the poor and Dalits, the Nepali people will not be able to tolerate it. I want to demand that the government investigate what happened, understand the facts of this incident, and inform the House. Thank you.
Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable member Nar Bahadur Bisht.
Honourable Mr. Nar Bahadur Bisht (Nepal Communist Party):- Honourable Chairperson, the inhumane and cruel act of this government, regarding Ganesh Nepali, a 25-year-old resident of Ward No. 1, Sora Rural Municipality, Mugu District, who, after locking his motorcycle in front of the Department of Passports yesterday, was asked for a fine of 10,000 rupees. After being asked, he asked his elder brother for the money, but his elder brother did not have it either. Then, out of compulsion, he doused himself with petrol and set himself on fire. Instead of saving him, the metropolitan police and the police present there dragged his vehicle, put him in a metropolitan vehicle, and took him to Bir Hospital, where we have just heard that he has died. This government seems to be a government of squatters, Dalits, landless, Madhesis, Muslims, and the poor; a demonic government that has come after burning the nation. It seems that those who burned the nation's property, burned history, are now creating a situation where the Nepali people are forced to rebel once again, wearing black glasses and black coats in the name of history. Therefore, I want to strongly condemn this government. If arbitrary actions are taken in the name of good governance, resistance will arise from the streets. Another matter, can a DSP Chaudhary say 'I am a police officer of the Government of Nepal'? Can he not say 'I am a police officer'? He is not a police officer of this government, but he is seen saying 'I am of the Government of Nepal', and for that, he is summoned to the district today. It seems that the Nepali people cannot tolerate such tyrannical and cruel rulers any longer. Therefore, I say again that Ganesh Nepali's incident requires an impartial investigation, and I want to offer my final heartfelt tribute to the victim and express my heartfelt condolences to the bereaved family. Therefore, I want to ask whether this new government will be held accountable for killing people in broad daylight? Will they be held accountable for murder? Thank you.
Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable member Somnath Poudel.
Honourable Mr. Somnath Poudel (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Honourable Chairperson, those who burned Singha Durbar have started burning the people after entering Singha Durbar. Today, a situation has been created where people have to burn themselves in broad daylight. I want to strongly condemn and denounce this. Ganesh Nepali, a resident of Ward No. 9, Ruru Rural Municipality, Mugu District, who was living in Kathmandu with his wife and three-year-old daughter, was providing services to the public through services like Pathao. For a small mistake of his, parking his motorcycle, the police imposed a fine of 10,000 rupees. He did not have the money to pay the fine. Because he did not have the money, he requested the police, saying he did not have the money, and the police took away his vehicle, his motorcycle. In that situation, a citizen who could not even afford his evening meal had to set himself on fire with petrol. I want to condemn and denounce this incident, and he has now passed away. I want to strongly condemn the government that created the circumstances for this death. Chairperson, the incident is not just this. The way a wounded patient was dragged and put into a vehicle by the police and taken to the hospital is a heartbreaking and brutal incident. I want to condemn and denounce this as well. Today, citizens are in a situation where they have to drown in rivers, where they have to set themselves on fire. I want to condemn and denounce the government that has created this situation. Why is this situation arising? Today, those who can commit the most atrocities against citizens, those who can cause the most suffering to citizens, are being rewarded. Those who can burn Singha Durbar by setting it on fire are being rewarded. Those who can cause the most suffering in the daily lives of the people, those who can operate bulldozers on people's houses, are being rewarded, and because of this, citizens, the poor, Dalits, squatters, and the landless have reached a state of statelessness. I want to warn the government by condemning this, and I urge the government to keep in mind that if it does not correct this situation, a situation will arise where the people's rebellion cannot be contained. Thank you.
Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable member Tul Prasad Bishwakarma.
Honourable Mr. Tul Prasad Bishwakarma (Rashtriya Janamorcha):- Honourable Chairperson, after the new government came to power, strange incidents are happening in the country. In some places, people are dying in custody. In some places, people kept in custody are dying. Today, a Pathao businessman has been forced to set himself on fire by pouring petrol on himself. This government has done extremely condemnable, sorrowful, and reprehensible work. For this, I want to condemn this government. He is an educated person, he has studied agriculture, and he has the certificate in his hand, but there is no employment. Therefore, he was earning a living for himself and his family by doing Pathao business. The incident happened last Thursday, in front of the Department of Passports in Tripureswor. When he parked his bike, the city police put a wheel lock on his bike, and when there was a dispute, he was forcibly issued a ticket, and it is said that a fine of 10,000 was demanded. He did not have the capacity to pay it, and he called his elder brother, but he could not arrange it from his elder brother either. Thus, out of helplessness, he committed self-immolation there. Instead of preventing the self-immolation, the police there watched as spectators instead of trying to save him, and after the self-immolation, he was put in their vehicle in a style of arrest and taken to the hospital, and he died a tragic death. Therefore, I want to tell this government that as our elders said, excess leads to ruin. May this government take heed of this, and if it oppresses the people, if it continues the severe oppression of the poor, the squatters, the helpless, the Dalits, and the minorities, it will have far-reaching adverse effects on the government. Thank you.
Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable members, the order of speaking during the zero hour concludes here. Honourable members, names have been registered to speak during the zero hour. I have set a time limit of 1 minute each for speaking during the zero hour. First, Honourable member Krishna Bahadur Rokaya.
Honourable Mr. Krishna Bahadur Rokaya (Nepali Congress):- Honourable Chairperson, a tragic incident occurred yesterday in Tripureswor. I first want to pay my heartfelt tribute to the late Nepali and express my condolences to the bereaved family. Honourable Chairperson, I want to strongly demand through you, the Honourable Chairperson, from the government that the government should conduct a fair investigation into the cause of this incident and his death, inform the House about this investigation, and take responsibility for the upbringing of the victim's family. Thank you.
Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable member Puja Chaudhary.
Honourable Ms. Puja Chaudhary (Janata Samajwadi Party, Nepal):- Honourable Chairperson, it is sad that the District Police Office, Kailali, has initiated a clarification and internal investigation process against DSP Prateek Raj Chaudhary of the Nepal Police due to remarks he made at a public event. I want to ask the government through you, the Honourable Chairperson, did a son of the indigenous, tribal, and native people showing his love for his country, and saying in his speech 'We are not Balen's police, we are Nepal Police', did he say something wrong? Is it a big crime to say 'I am Nepal Police'? A person in public office belongs to the country, not to anyone personally. The government does not see the tears of the squatters, does not see the pain of farmers not receiving fertilizer, but a true patriotic soldier is called for clarification for what he said. Alas, my country, excess conquers all. Nothing should be done in excess. I want to ask the government through you, the Honourable Chairperson, what kind of good governance is this, which has pushed Ganesh Nepali to the brink of death and Prateek Raj Chaudhary (. Time expired..).
Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable member Manrupa Sharma.
Honourable Ms. Manrupa Sharma (Nepal Communist Party):- Honourable Chairperson, Ganesh Nepali, a 24-year-old from Sora Rural Municipality-1, Mugu, who reached the state's doorstep to get a passport, died during treatment at Bir Hospital. I want to express my heartfelt tribute to Ganesh Nepali and extend my condolences to his relatives and family. I also want to thank this Balen government. It is not just the death of one youth, but the murder of youth, the government is murdering thousands of youths. It is the fire of self-respect ignited by the state on the hopes and trust of the people. Today, the issue is not just about one Ganesh Nepali, but about thousands of youths who are insulted, disappointed, and in pain at the state's doorstep. I demand that the government conduct an impartial investigation into the incident and take action against the guilty. I strongly demand that the government ensure accountable governance, not punitive rule, over citizens.

Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Member Rukmini Koirala.
(1:35 PM)
Honorable Mr. Rukmini Koirala (Communist Party of Nepal, UML):-
(1:34 PM)
Honorable Chairperson, when the state becomes insensitive and rulers lose their conscience, the soul of the country and society dies. Ganesh Nepali, 25, who attempted self-immolation at the Passport Department, and Jivan, a resident of Bhaktapur, originally from Soru Rural Municipality Ward No. 3 in Mugu district, who drives a Pathao for a living, had his motorcycle locked by the Metropolitan City while driving, and due to lack of alternatives, he was forced to self-immolate. Sir, Ganesh Nepali has died. I express my condolences to him and ask the government. Honorable Members, the ministry-wise question and answer session will now begin. Honorable Members, after the Honorable Minister responds, if the questioning Honorable Member wishes, they may ask a supplementary question related to their question within 1 minute. Honorable Members, I invite Honorable Minister of Agriculture, Forest and Environment, Gita Chaudhary, to the rostrum to answer the questions posed by the Honorable Member.
Honorable Members, I now provide time to the questioning Honorable Member Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" to ask her question.
Honorable Mr. Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" (Communist Party of Nepal):-
(1:46 PM)
Honorable Chairperson, through you, my question to the Honorable Minister is as follows: What is the reason for the conflict between nature conservation and development? And how can this conflict be resolved policy-wise, and how can both activities be carried out simultaneously by maintaining harmony between conservation and development, leading to equitable development of the country? The Public Policy and Good Governance Legislation Committee had studied the policy problems related to national parks and submitted a report with suggestions to the National Assembly. The report suggested modifications to the policy related to national parks in 35 points. On 2082 Magh 23, in the 18th meeting of the 19th session of the National Assembly, the report was discussed. After the discussion, the Honorable Chairperson directed the government to implement the suggestions based on the views expressed by the Honorable Minister in response and the report. What steps has the government taken to implement the recommendations suggested in the said study report? Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Minister.
(1:47 PM)
Honorable Minister of Agriculture, Forest and Environment, Ms. Gita Chaudhary:- Honorable
(1:47 PM)
Sir, Honorable Members, the issue raised by Honorable Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" is relevant and important. I will not go into the question, but will go directly to the answer. I wish to inform you that the report of the Public Policy Study Subcommittee, chaired by the Honorable Member, was discussed and amended by the Public Policy and Good Governance Legislation Committee and presented to the National Assembly, and after discussion, the government was directed to implement the suggestions mentioned in the report. The suggestions are in the process of being implemented. As suggested in the report, national parks are sensitive areas, so by managing them with a focus on conservation and maintaining ecological integrity, and by facilitating the use of forest products in conservation areas and buffer zones, an amendment bill to the National Parks and Wildlife Conservation Act, 2029 has been prepared and the regulations are in the process of being amended. Specifically, work is being done in accordance with the 100-point agenda of the Government of Nepal, including the 10-point action plan of the former Ministry of Forest and Environment. Furthermore, the process of simplifying the operation of small and cottage industries on private land within the buffer zone and conservation area has been simplified. The Ministry has facilitated infrastructure development projects, including hydropower, for which survey permits were obtained before 2081 Asar 24, as decided by the Council of Ministers on 2082 Mangsir 8 and is being implemented. It has been proposed to amend the Act to allow local levels to collect and distribute riverbed materials from rivers, excluding forest areas and important aquatic ecosystems within the buffer zone, based on environmental studies. It is requested that special programs and budget allocations be made for local levels within the buffer zone. As per the recommendations of the report, the amendment to the National Parks and Wildlife Conservation Act will propose the establishment of a Wildlife Conservation Fund to manage human-wildlife conflict, rescue wildlife, and carry out other conservation activities. The possibility of including the human and property damage caused by wildlife in the insurance system is being studied by the Insurance Authority.

It is being done. I want to inform you that a proposal has been prepared to allow the Government of Nepal to issue orders related to the control of wildlife crime, to improve the directive on relief distribution for damage caused by wildlife, and to modify the intermediate zone management regulations to enhance the role of local levels in the intermediate zone. It is necessary to construct wildlife-friendly infrastructure with special attention to sensitive areas and biological corridors, and the red monkey and wild boar have been declared harmful to agriculture across Nepal for one year. A draft of the criteria for establishing and operating zoos, wildlife rescue centers, and wildlife hospitals has been prepared. This will be taken to the approval process and implemented. I want to inform you that internal preparations and efforts are underway to resolve the problems of those displaced during the expansion of Shuklaphanta National Park. Thus, considering the report overall, the Ministry is committed to implementing the important suggestions included in the report by improving and amending the relevant laws, acts, and regulations, and by paying attention to programs and budget allocation and making necessary arrangements. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Members, now the questioner (13:51 hrs) Honorable Member wishes to ask a supplementary question, so I will provide time to ask a supplementary question focused on the subject. Honorable Member Ms. Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" (Nepal Communist Party):- (13:51 hrs) With due respect to the Honorable Minister through the Honorable Chairperson, I wish to ask a supplementary question. Honorable Minister, you yourself are from Shuklaphanta National Park. It has been more than 22 years since the park was established, and the displaced people from the district where the park is located have not been managed. When will these displaced people be managed justly? I want to ask a supplementary question about what the government's plan is. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Minister. (13:52 hrs) Honorable Minister of Agriculture, Forest and Environment, Ms. Gita Chaudhary:- Honorable Chairperson, Honorable Members, I wish to answer the question asked by the Honorable Member. I myself am from Shuklaphanta National Park, and perhaps many of the victims there are my own relatives. I know about the problem since I was in the fourth or fifth grade when that movement, when they were displaced. I am also aware of the problem. I am taking many steps to provide justice to them in the position I am in now. I want to inform you that this is not only under my ministry but is interconnected with other relevant ministries, and my Ministry of Agriculture, Forest and Environment and the Ministry of Land Management are jointly making efforts. We have just formed a study committee. It includes the work done by all the commissions so far, and there is dissatisfaction among the victims regarding the work done by those commissions. We have formed a committee to address their dissatisfaction regarding the matters studied by those commissions. After we confirm those processes, the Ministry of Land Management will take over and move forward with the process of land distribution. We have announced that we will solve land-related problems within 500 days this time. I want to inform you that we are committed to solving the problems of the victims within Shuklaphanta National Park within that time. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Members, now I provide time to Honorable Member Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma to ask his question. Honorable Member Mr. Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma (Nepal Communist Party):- (13:54 hrs) Honorable Chairperson, through the Honorable Chairperson, I want to ask a question to the Honorable Minister. Considering the direct impact of climate change on marginalized communities such as Dalits, Janajatis, and Sukumbasis, what is the status of the utilization, distribution, and use of carbon benefits and royalty amounts received through programs implemented by Nepal such as climate victim management, health security, disaster risk reduction, and resilient livelihoods, as well as forests and other means, on a provincial basis? How is the participation and benefit sharing of indigenous peoples, Janajatis, Dalits, and disaster-affected communities in those programs? And what policy and financial management structures have been implemented to ensure that climate funds and disaster relief adaptation budgets effectively reach the local levels? I request clarification. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Minister. (13:54 hrs) Honorable Minister of Agriculture, Forest and Environment, Ms. Gita Chaudhary:- Honorable Chairperson, Honorable Members, regarding the question raised by Honorable Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma, the Ministry of Agriculture, Forest and Environment has taken note. The issue he raised is very relevant and important in the current context. Nepal is a nation with high climate risk despite low carbon emissions, and considering the social and economic diversity from the mountains, hills, and plains, as well as women, children, youth, elderly citizens, Dalits, and persons with disabilities, the following climate-related policies and plans are clearly addressed in the following explanations. It will be a bit long because I am going into detail about our policies that encompass all communities. Firstly, among the four main cross-cutting areas of the National Climate Change Policy, 2076, in Section 8.9 on Gender Equality and Social Inclusion, Livelihood, and Good Governance, the following policies, strategies, and action plans are mentioned. Policy: Equal participation and just rights of women, indigenous peoples, Janajatis, Madhesis, Dalits, oppressed classes, persons with disabilities, and youth in climate change programs will be ensured. Strategies and Action Plans: The gender and social inclusion perspective will be mandatorily mainstreamed in the formulation of every plan for climate adaptation and mitigation. The meaningful participation of women and disaster-affected classes in natural resource management and decision-making processes will be increased. Similarly, in Section 10.2 of the policy on Financial Management, resources will be mobilized from international mechanisms such as the Green Climate Fund (GCF) and the Global Environment Facility (GEF) to increase access to climate finance. It is mentioned that at least 80 percent of the climate budget received from national and international sources will be spent directly on local-level program implementation. The National Adaptation Plan (NAP) is for 2021 to 2050, and Section 7.9 of this plan, Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), Livelihood, and Governance, is directly related to the equal participation and just rights of women, indigenous peoples, Janajatis, Madhesis, Dalits, oppressed classes, persons with disabilities, and youth. Climate risks and vulnerabilities, as well as adaptation programs and action plans, have been determined accordingly. The objectives of Gender Equality, Disability, and Social Inclusion (GESI) and Just Transition Principles are to ensure equal access to resources, means, services, and decision-making processes for all individuals, and to appropriately include their diverse perspectives, needs, and priorities in policies and programs. Nepal has adopted the principles of Just Transition to implement relevant policies and measures to achieve the goals of inclusive Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC). Another matter is Nepal's Long-Term Strategy for Net Zero Emission, which embraces the principles of Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) and 'Leave no one behind' equality, ensuring equal access and meaningful participation in resources, means, services, opportunities, and decision-making processes for women, children, youth, indigenous peoples, persons with disabilities, homosexuals, lesbians, gay men, bisexuals, transgender, queer, and other marginalized and deprived communities. The Carbon Trading Regulations, 2082. Rule 18 of the regulations deals with the distribution of benefits from carbon trading. Along with this, the provincial status of the mobilization, distribution, and utilization of carbon benefits obtained from forest carbon trading is as follows: First, the carbon project (FCPF) agreement with the World Bank. In this, 13 districts of the Terai plains, Rautahat, Parsa, Bara in Madhesh, Nawalpur in Gandaki, Chitwan in Bagmati, Rupandehi, Kapilvastu, Dang, Banke, Bardiya, Nawalparasi in Lumbini, Kailali, Kanchanpur in Sudurpashchim, have signed agreements with the World Bank for carbon sales from 2018 to 2024 and have been implemented. By implementing this program, Nepal has prepared an emission reduction project "People and Forests: A Sustainable Forest Management-Based Emission Reduction Program in the Terai Arc Landscape, Nepal" covering 13 districts of the Terai plains, from Rautahat to Kanchanpur, and in the first phase from 2018 to 2021, the third-party certification has been completed, and an amount of USD 9.4 million, equivalent to 1 billion 340 million rupees, has been received. The approved benefit sharing plan of the FCPF project has a system for benefit distribution as follows: 10 percent for forest development fund management expenses, and 70 percent for other bodies, REDD implementation centers, and forest research and training centers, and 30 percent for the Department of Forest and Soil Conservation, making it 100 percent. I want to inform you that I have explained this 100 percent of 10 percent. Similarly, 80 percent is for the distribution between the emission reduction committee and the beneficiaries who have made direct contributions, and this 80 percent is divided into forest user groups, division forest offices, national park buffer zones, and results-based shares. Furthermore, 4 percent is for private forest owners, managed through local levels, and 4 percent is for forest-dependent communities not affiliated with groups. I want to inform you that this is managed through the REDD implementation center and provincial bodies as per Rule 114 of the Forest Regulations, Benefit Sharing Plan, 2024 Investment Plan. Similarly, I want to inform you that special arrangements have been made for Dalits, indigenous peoples, Janajatis, and Dalit communities as follows: For intermediate community forests and user groups of community forests, 35 percent for forest conservation and management, 34 percent for human-wildlife management, and 30 percent for capacity development and conservation-targeted livelihoods. Similarly, from the share received by user groups for livelihoods and capacity development, 40 percent is for women, 24 percent for indigenous Janajatis, 10 percent for Madhesis, and for Dalits.

for targeted programs and implementation, and similarly, 40 percent of the allocated budget from the National Parks Office and Forest Division Office will be allocated to consumer groups, indigenous communities, Dalit communities, women's groups, organizations, minority groups, agroforestry groups, livestock groups, herb farming groups, and other beneficiary groups to support conservation and sustainable management through capacity building, forest enterprise, ecotourism, livelihood based on traditional knowledge and skills, pasture management, agroforestry, organic farming, and human-wildlife conflict mitigation, and multi-use of water. Similarly, the FCPF Carbon Project will operate based on performance, providing benefits to beneficiaries according to the approved benefit-sharing plan. The first phase, from 2018 to 2021, was certified by a third party, and as I informed earlier, an amount of 9.4 million (1.34 billion) was received, and based on that, the benefit-sharing was determined and registered in the LMBIS with the program. Regarding carbon emission reduction, this is the LEAF Coalition Project in 36 districts of Bagmati, Gandaki, and Lumbini provinces. The Government of Nepal and Emergent signed an agreement on January 21, 2026, to sell carbon from 2022 to 2026, and it has been implemented. The benefit-sharing plan for this program is currently in the draft preparation stage. Currently, Rule 115 of the Forest Regulations has the following provision. This caste came to Nepal as a dowry of the Rana regime for their care. I am expressing my opinion that this should also be studied, and this report is not complete, it needs to be completed. Thank you.

Honorable Chairperson: Honorable member Suresh Kumar Ale Magar, followed by (15:01 hrs) Honorable member Roshi Mechhe.

Honorable Mr. Suresh Kumar Ale Magar (Nepal Communist Party): Honorable Chairperson, today we are discussing the National Inclusion Commission, and I am also present at this rostrum in this regard. First of all, the discussion of the National Inclusion Commission, one of the constitutional bodies, has started in the National Assembly, and this is a historic act. For this historic act and creativity, I want to express my heartfelt thanks and gratitude to the Honorable Chairperson. Because the reports of constitutional bodies are presented in the National Assembly, some read them, some don't, they take them, they know, but they are presented, discussions are not held. What is the point of discussing? Why are discussions not held after the discussion is presented? What is the justification for holding discussions? Such questions arise, however, this act that has happened is a very correct and historic act, and while stating this, I want to go into a little history about this commission.

Honorable Chairperson, I was also in the Constituent Assembly formed in 2064 BS. At that time, among various committees, there was a committee called the Constitutional Body Nomination Determination Committee. Govinda Chaudhary was the chairperson of that committee, and I was also a member. This is a happy coincidence for me. I also got the opportunity to work with the chairperson of the committee at that time, who was a father. Currently, his daughter is in the National Assembly, and I have the opportunity to work with her. Speaking from personal experience, I have realized that it feels more difficult than a khukuri. After this, Honorable Chairperson, what I want to say is that this commission, although it is called inclusive, is actually non-inclusive. Because it has representation from only one caste. Ram Krishna Timilsina, Chairperson; he has retired; Haridatta Joshi, Pushparaj Timilsina, Vishnu Ojha, members; Man Bahadur Khatri, member. There is a lot to be said here. Bahun Chhetri, backward class, persons with disabilities, senior citizens, etc., etc. Due to lack of time, I don't want to go into that. But therefore, this commission itself does not seem inclusive, and if we believe the statements of the officials of this commission, their statement was: You have your own commissions. There is the Indigenous Nationalities Commission, the Dalit Commission, the Madhesi Commission, the Muslim Commission. What about the Bahun Chhetri? they asked. Therefore, in their own words, this is such a commission, I don't want to use this word here. Anyway, this commission, which has been allocated a budget of 4 crore 32 lakh 16 thousand 507, held 20 various meetings last year. Similarly, it conducted review, discussion, interaction, monitoring, etc., programs and also published a souvenir. It has given many policy recommendations, and it is said that many of them have been implemented.

An honorable member said earlier that many of its recommendations, the recommendations of this commission, have been implemented. We have read in the कैफियत (kaifiyat - report/details) that the recommendations of other commissions have not been implemented. But it is found that many recommendations of this commission have been implemented. Perhaps it is because of the structure of the commission's officials? I don't know. Is it because the recommendations are made by them, from the same community, and implemented by the same community, or what, I don't know. But anyway, it is found that many recommendations have been made. It has also presented many problems and challenges. Similarly, it has also conducted a comparative study of indigenous and tribal peoples. Although this is not a meeting, regarding the basis of identity, it seems to me that anyone can study the various ethnic communities of Nepal. There is no need to define its scope of work. But still, there were others to study this, one thing. What is its most negative aspect is that in last year's report, it recommended that reservation is not necessary from the year 2091 BS. This is a condemnable proposal, this commission also made this highly objectionable proposal and recommendation. If this commission makes such recommendations, such an inclusive commission, only one...

There is no need for a commission for caste. When such commissions are formed, the relevance and importance of such bodies are questioned. Therefore, I would like to heartily request the current officials of this commission to remember this. If the recommendations made by various commissions cannot be implemented by the Government of Nepal, they must be implemented, and if they cannot be implemented, they must explain why. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Roshni Mechhe. Then Honorable Member Shree Krishna Prasad Adhikari. Honorable Shree Roshni Mechhe (Nepal Communist Party, UML): Honorable Chairperson, first of all, I would like to express my happiness that the work of discussing the report of the Constitutional Commission has begun in this responsible National Assembly, and I would also like to express my thanks to the Honorable Chairperson for taking the initiative for this work. I am confident that the start of this work will make the work of the Constitutional Commission even more responsible and effective. Today, we are discussing the seventh report submitted by the National Inclusion Commission. This commission is also directly linked to Nepal's economic and social transformation. What is the current status of the National Inclusion Commission, as stipulated by Article 248 of Part 27 of the Constitution of Nepal? Chairperson, there is a bitter reality in the report: the constitution has given this commission a large area of work to change the lives of Khas Arya, backward classes, senior citizens, persons with disabilities, laborers, farmers, and the oppressed people of Karnali. As vast as the area of work is, the resources, budget, and manpower provided by the government are equally small. How can inclusion be successful with such policies? I want to ask the government, how many decisions has the government made on the important policy recommendations and suggestions given by the commission? Why do the commission's reports only gather dust in the drawers of Singha Durbar? If the government is going to throw the recommendations of the constitutional commissions into the dustbin, then what is the purpose of forming these commissions? Chairperson, we chant the slogan of a prosperous Nepal, but is development possible without bringing women, who constitute more than half the sky, senior citizens, marginalized people from remote areas, minorities, and farmers and laborers, who are considered the backbone of the nation, into the mainstream of the state? Will citizens left behind based on geography and ethnicity live hungry and thirsty, while speeches of prosperity are delivered from palaces in Kathmandu, is this our socialist-oriented federal democratic republic? Absolutely not. Until the last citizen of the country feels that the state is theirs, the foundation of Nepal's true development cannot be laid. Chairperson, if we look at international practices, such as the Equality Commission of South Africa or the special constitutional bodies created for marginalized classes in India, the directives given by these commissions are binding on the government. We have the example of South Africa taking significant steps to reduce its economic inequality Gini coefficient by implementing inclusive laws. In Nepal too, as long as the Inclusion Commission cannot work independently by connecting with a digital data bank and local governments, we will remain backward. Chairperson, for a multilingual, multi-ethnic, and geographically diverse country like Nepal, inclusion is not a matter of mercy or charity; it is the only infallible formula to prevent the country from disintegrating and to strengthen national unity. Therefore, the National Inclusion Commission must be provided with adequate budget, manpower, and resources immediately to establish its strong administrative presence in all seven provinces, and I want the government to monitor whether the commission's recommendations are being implemented or not and to inform the public. Otherwise, if all the recommendations made by the commission are just written declarations on paper, the stomach of inclusivity will not be filled, nor will the faces of the people of Karnali smile. Let us think in time and move forward by including everyone in the journey of prosperity. I want to say this, I want to present this. This is also seen in this report. The lack of budget has already come up. It is also seen in this report that the benefits of inclusion have been repeatedly taken by a limited number of people. The commission also needs to pay special attention to how this can be implemented in a way that fulfills the spirit of inclusion, and the government also needs to seriously consider and implement all the recommendations made by the commission. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Shree Krishna Prasad Adhikari. Then Honorable Member Somnath Pörtel. Honorable Shree Krishna Prasad Adhikari (Nepali Communist Party): Honorable Chairperson, I would like to express my heartfelt thanks to the Honorable Chairperson of the National Assembly, the Ministers of the Government of Nepal, and all the staff of the Parliament for initiating the new process of discussing the annual report of the National Inclusion Commission for the first time in this esteemed assembly. The commission has defined its work, duties, and responsibilities in accordance with Article 259 of the Constitution and the National Inclusion Commission Act, 2074, and has made the directive principles of the state, fundamental rights, state policy, and the goals of sustainable development, the policies and programs determined by the government's periodic plans, and international commitments as the main basis for its performance. Along with the breadth of its work, it has also identified problems such as lack of budget and necessary manpower, weak physical infrastructure, insufficient development of understanding regarding the implementation of issues recommended by the commission, and lack of positive perception towards the commission. It is clear to us that this commission itself has not been inclusive in its formation, nor have its activities progressed according to inclusive processes. While the commission's mandate includes ensuring meaningful access of ethnic, religious, linguistic diversity and oppressed minority communities, geographically, politically, economically, and socially backward marginalized, extremely marginalized, and endangered communities to governance, advancing their economic transformation, and working impartially for all, the focus seems to have narrowed. Therefore, Honorable Chairperson, as the country's political landscape has become increasingly difficult for the poor in recent times, further inclusion is needed for the commission. The gaps of discrimination, oppression, and inequality based on class, ethnicity, region, economy, and culture are still widening. The current government has not been satisfactory in providing suggestions for changing the economic lives of the basic classes by solving the housing, education, and employment problems of women, Dalits, Muslims, Khas Arya, backward classes, persons with disabilities, senior citizens, laborers, farmers, workers, minorities and marginalized communities, and neglected populations of Karnali, Madhesh, remote hilly, and Himalayan regions, landless squatters, and unmanaged settlers, and in focusing its work in that direction. In the middle of the monsoon, the homeless squatters have been evicted and left stranded on the streets. A Pao driver who wants to earn a living within the country is forced to commit suicide in broad daylight due to an inability to bear the burden of fines and taxes. In this situation, I want to draw attention to making the Inclusion Commission more accountable and responsible by restructuring the commission itself and also making the government accountable. I would like to draw the government's attention to implementing some of the suggestions given by the National Inclusion Commission to make the government vigilant, such as providing assistance to severely disabled individuals. I conclude by drawing attention to these matters. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Somnath Pörtel. Then Honorable Member Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma. Honorable Shree Somnath Pörtel (Nepal Communist Party, UML): Honorable Chairperson, we are discussing the seventh annual report of the National Inclusion Commission. I would like to express my heartfelt thanks to the Honorable Chairperson for the time. And I would like to express my heartfelt thanks to the Honorable Chairperson for initiating a new tradition of discussing the annual reports of constitutional bodies. Chairperson, the National Inclusion Commission seems to be coming up with something, given its form. Given its form, I am saying 'Inclusion Commission' very cautiously, fearing that it might become difficult again. It has a wide scope, including economic poverty, and minority communities. If it is to work within its actual scope, I have looked at where this commission should go first, and that is to the Dalit settlements. Because if there is anyone who is the poorest in Nepal, it is the Dalit. So, where is its scope of work? It is among the poor. About 20 percent of Nepal's population is below the absolute poverty line, and more than 33 percent of that population is Dalit. So, if there are 2 million Dalits among the approximately 6 million people living below the absolute poverty line, then if it is to work among the poor, the first task it must do is to work among the Dalits. Second, minorities. Among the oppressed Dalit communities, there are about 25 castes, of which 19 are minorities. So, if it is to work among minorities, it seems it has to work among the Dalit community. However, I would like to urge the commission to pay special attention to where the commission's work is heading. The commission has done a lot of work. Despite limited resources and manpower, the commission has done a lot of work. It studied about 14 topics in the last fiscal year, gave two suggestions, and made seven recommendations. Similarly, it conducted interaction discussions with more than 15 local levels, provinces, and the center. Therefore, in terms of these works, it seems the commission has done a lot, including seven additional studies and observations on the state of inclusion. Thus, looking at the work, it appears the commission has done a lot. However, I would like to draw attention to the fact that the commission may need to reconsider where to focus its work. The commission itself says that the implementation of its recommendations is weak, so the commission's appropriate recommendations must be implemented. However, if the commission makes recommendations of this nature, I cannot stand here and say that they must be implemented. For example, it made a recommendation, the study report on the reservation system, 2079, which recommended abolishing the reservation system from 2091. Chairperson, what is the basis of discrimination in our country? Is it class-based or caste-based? The basis of discrimination is caste, it is based on varna, there is discrimination based on varna, which has marginalized people, and if you implement reservation and inclusion based on varna, its treatment will not be correct. The system of reservation is not something we have implemented today. I want to remind you that in Nepal, more than today...

Reservation has existed for 1500 years. Who gets to study? Everyone knows, right? In this country, only Brahmins can study. Only Kshatriyas can rule. Only Dalits can do service work. From sewing shoes, making tools, to sewing clothes, only Dalits can do service work. Only Brahmins can study and write, only Kshatriyas can rule the state, only Vaishyas can do business, so isn't this a reservation system? Is this reservation system something that has been in place only since 2063 BS? At that time, we only tried to slightly amend the existing reservation system, we tried to make it a little more democratic. Therefore, the reservation system has existed in Nepal for 1500 years. That system has left a community, a class behind today, so we want to change it in a new way, so let the commission's work be focused in this direction, thank you.

Presiding Officer: Respected Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
(15:18 hrs)
Respected Chairperson:- Honorable Member Mr. Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma.
(15:23 hrs)
Honorable Mr. Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma (Nepal Communist Party):
(15:23 hrs)
Respected Chairperson Sir, first of all, I would like to thank the Respected Chairperson. The discussion on the reports of the commissions has started, this is a historic work. We used to get and read the reports of these commissions, but it is not enough for us to read them, the public also needs to understand and know this, so I thank you for starting this. Secondly, today is like a dark day for us, due to the negligence of the Balen government, a promising youth, a very promising youth has lost his life. He had to sacrifice his life prematurely. Therefore, as a person from that place, from that cluster, I am in immense pain today. I would like to pay heartfelt tribute to Ganesh Nepali, who was forced to die in this painful situation, and I express deep condolences to the bereaved family. Ganesh Nepali was forced to die by the people of the Balen government because he could not pay a bribe of ten thousand rupees. They tortured him for two and a half hours, and finally forced him to die. They dragged him to the hospital after he was already burnt. This cruel government, I say again, has no right to be in power; if there is any morality, leave the seat and go. Respected Chairperson Sir, we are currently discussing the report of the National Inclusion Commission. I had the opportunity to read this report cursorily, and I read the report. Although it is called the Constitutional National Inclusion Commission, the name is inclusive, but its form is not inclusive, it is exclusive. Either its name should be changed, or it should be made inclusive in character. This mistake might not be of this government, perhaps the previous government created it. Let's hope that mistake doesn't happen again. Therefore, I have this much to say about this inclusive commission and its form. Furthermore, its scope of work is broad, large, and long, but it seems to want to do a lot of work, but it is not clear here how seriously the government has taken its recommendations, and the complaint that the government has not taken them seriously is found in this report. Therefore, by changing its structural form and arranging for capable manpower, its physical infrastructure, the office's physical infrastructure, is also painful, so the government should also pay attention to the physical infrastructure. It studies and researches, especially for the Dalit community and others, and makes recommendations, which is good. And another thing, it also researches and makes recommendations on whether Karnali residents have access and representation in the government machinery. Therefore, it will make recommendations on how much representation and access Karnali residents have in the government and its machinery. It is understood that the implementation of those recommendations is not confirmed here. On the other hand, it also determines the curriculum for inclusivity in school education. Therefore, it must have determined the curriculum and made recommendations. Although it has not been implemented yet, let it be implemented. As I said before, the government should implement its building, the budget it demands, and the recommendations it has made. The government should take it seriously and implement it. The government must give work to the commissions we have formed, and make their work meaningful. Therefore, the problem of budget and manpower is seen here. Let the manpower be fulfilled, let the budget be fulfilled, thus I end my statement. Thank you.

Respected Chairperson:- Honorable Members, the discussion on the proposal to discuss the annual report of the National Inclusion Commission for the fiscal year 2080/81 in the assembly is now concluded.

Honorable Members, now I provide time to the Honorable Minister of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Sovita Gautam, from the side of the Right Honorable Prime Minister Balendra Shah, to respond to the questions raised in the discussion.

Honorable Minister of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Ms. Sovita Gautam:-
(15:29 hrs)
Respected Chairperson Sir, for the first time today, a discussion on the report of a constitutional commission has taken place in the National Assembly. This is a very new practice in our parliamentary practice. We have been extensively discussing this matter in the Business Committee as well. In principle, since constitutional commissions are formed by the executive, our accountability is limited only to the implementation of the recommendations made by our constitutional commissions. Therefore, I would like to inform you all that the government is committed to seriously implementing all our commission reports and the recommendations given by them. We are observing, some things are happening gradually, some are in the process of happening, some require new laws, some require behavioral improvements, we will continue to do so. The issues you have raised today are also very appropriate. We will incorporate the theoretical aspects and the issues raised into the places that need improvement. Now, the accountability of the constitutional commission is the federal parliament, as written in the constitution, and since it has a somewhat independent nature from the government, the government's accountability is theoretically somewhat mismatched. Therefore, I have taken the issues raised here seriously, and in the future, we will make improvements where and where they are needed. If discussions on constitutional commissions can be more focused in committees, it would be appropriate to call the officials there and discuss, it would be double-sided, the government will know where to improve, and the commission officials will also be there. A framework will also emerge on how the work is progressing. Perhaps a committee of this nature should be formed, or how it should be done? This debate, I feel, has also started a beginning in that regard with today's National Assembly discussion. I feel the debate has started. For this, I express my gratitude to the National Assembly and the Respected Chairperson. Now, regarding the rest, how we can improve, we have our formal and informal forums. I have taken the issues raised here seriously, and with this, I would like to conclude my remarks, Respected Chairperson Sir, thank you.

Respected Chairperson:- Honorable Members, the discussion on the annual report of the National Inclusion Commission for the fiscal year 2080/081 is now concluded. Honorable Members, the serious discussion with the active participation of the Honorable Members in today's meeting, and the response given by the Honorable Minister of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Sovita Gautam, on behalf of the Government of Nepal, regarding the issues raised during the discussion, has not only made this discussion meaningful and successful, but it will also pave the way for the procedure of discussions on the reports of other constitutional bodies in the future and will further refine this process. The Government of Nepal will pay serious attention to the implementation of the suggestions and recommendations mentioned in the commission's report and the appropriate addressing and implementation of the issues raised by the Honorable Members during the discussion in the assembly.

Honorable Members, the next meeting of the National Assembly will be held on Wednesday, Asar 31, 2083, at 1:15 PM, and this meeting is hereby adjourned.

(Thereafter, the next meeting will be held on Wednesday, Asar 31, 2083, at 1:15 PM, and this meeting is hereby adjourned.)

sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Roshni Mechhe initiated a discussion on the report of the National Inclusion Commission, highlighting the disparity between the commission's broad mandate and the limited resources allocated by the government. She questioned the effectiveness of inclusion policies when recommendations are ignored and emphasized the need for the government to implement suggestions and provide adequate resources to the commission. Honorable Member Shree Krishna Prasad Adhikari thanked the assembly for initiating the discussion on the commission's report and outlined the commission's mandate and identified challenges such as lack of budget, manpower, and weak implementation of recommendations. He also pointed out the commission's narrow focus and the widening gap of inequality in the country, urging for greater accountability from both the commission and the government.

sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Somnath Pörtel discussed the National Inclusion Commission's seventh annual report, thanking the chair for the new discussion format. He emphasized the commission's broad scope, including poverty and minority issues, and suggested focusing on Dalit communities as the poorest segment of the population. He acknowledged the commission's work despite resource limitations but urged reconsideration of its focus. He also questioned the recommendation to abolish reservations, arguing that discrimination is primarily caste-based and requires a different approach.
